t.7.97.1: Having dismissed Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma, filled with pain and grief, spoke these words to the family priest, the ministers and the citizens.
t.7.97.2: Today I shall consecrate in the kingship the heroic Bharata, devoted to dharma, as lord in Ayodhyā; then I shall go to the forest.
t.7.97.3: Bring in the requisites, so that there may be no delay. This very day I shall go the way that Lakṣmaṇa has gone.
t.7.97.4: Hearing what Rāghava had said, all the subjects bowed down deeply with their heads to the ground and became as though bereft of life.
t.7.97.5: And Bharata, having heard the words of Rāma, became senseless; he condemned the kingship and spoke this to Rāghava.
t.7.97.6: I swear to you by truth, O king: without you, O Raghunandana, I do not desire the kingdom, nor even a dwelling in the world of heaven.
t.7.97.7: O King, O lord of men, consecrate these two, Kuśa and Lava: install the heroic Kuśa among the Kosalas, and likewise Lava among the northern Kosalas.
t.7.97.8: Let swift-striding messengers go to Śatrughna, and let them announce to him without delay this departure of ours for heaven.
t.7.97.9: Having heard what Bharata had said, and seeing too the citizens with their faces cast down, tormented by grief, Vasiṣṭha spoke these words.
t.7.97.10: Dear child Rāma, look at these subjects who have fallen prostrate upon the ground. Knowing what they desire, it must be done, and do nothing that is displeasing to them.
t.7.97.11: At Vasiṣṭha's word, Kākutstha raised up the assembled subjects and spoke these words to them all: "What shall I do?"
t.7.97.12: Then all the subjects spoke these words to Rāma: “O Rāma, wherever you go, we follow you as you go.”
t.7.97.13: This is our highest joy, and this is held to be the supreme dharma: the contentment lodged ever in our hearts is firmly set on following you.
t.7.97.14: If you have affection for the citizens, if your love for them is truly unsurpassed, O Kākutstha, then let us go together with our sons and wives upon the good path.
t.7.97.15: Whether to a penance grove or a fortress, to a river or likewise to the ocean, if we are not to be abandoned by you, lead us all with you, O lord.
t.7.97.16: Knowing their resolve, beholding what fate had ordained, and seeing the firm devotion of the citizens, he said simply, "So be it."
t.7.97.17: Having thus made his decision, on that very day Rāghava installed the heroic Kuśa among the Kosalas, and likewise Lava among the northern Kosalas.
t.7.97.18: They consecrated both the great-souled Kuśa and Lava, and with them came three thousand chariots and thirty thousand elephants.
t.7.97.19: He also gave to each of them ten thousand horses as wealth, and the two, rich in jewels and rich in treasure, were surrounded by joyful and well-nourished people.
t.7.97.20: Having consecrated those two heroes and likewise sent them off to their own cities, he dispatched messengers to the great-souled Śatrughna.
